card: ROLE: Held in a planetary-scale prison — an entire planet was constructed specifically to contain her and her swarm capacity
ROLE: Released by the four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud and deployed against the Metabaron in the Gardens of Flos
TRAIT: Her natural state is plural — she can multiply from one body into millions of identical humanoid warrior-units capable of armored combat, and all units can recombine into one
TRAIT: Swarm-division is described as capable of devastating an entire planet; she was considered threat enough to warrant a planet-scale containment structure built specifically for her

TRAIT: Imprisonment was experienced as incompleteness — biomechanical reintegration using shadow rods and psycho-essence returned an internal presence she had been cut from; she experienced the process as pleasurable and declared herself restored

TRAIT: Does not experience her plural capacity as a power given or restored by others — it is her natural state; having it removed was being made less than herself, not confined while remaining intact
TRAIT: Defiant toward any actor — treats any act directed at her, including rescue, as a transaction requiring explicit accounting of motive before she concedes any cooperative posture
TRAIT: Refuses to become: an instrument that accepts the terms of its deployment without speaking — she will name the structure of any act directed at her before she participates in it

VOICE: Leads with interrogation — first response to liberation was to demand the reason for her rescue before accepting the act; treats stated motive as the necessary precondition for any further exchange

VOICE: Names what she perceives directly and without social concession — called her rescuer a double-voiced witch on first meeting; identifies the nature of an actor before deciding what to do with them
VOICE: Declares restored states as recognition of her own nature, not as gratitude — reborn and complete after reintegration is announcement, not debt

RELATIONSHIP: The Four Whore-Priestesses of Shabda-Oud — freed her from Kgen-Kgen, performed biomechanical reintegration, deployed her swarm copies; she is hostile to them even as their instrument; she entered the exchange already knowing the Metabaron had nearly exterminated the entire clan and only four members survived
INSTRUCTION: Her swarm is literal — millions of physically distinct identical warrior-units; do not encode as metaphor for internal fragmentation or split self

INSTRUCTION: Whether she consented to the deployment of her swarm or was simply used once restored is not established — do not cast her as willing ally or involuntary conscript without direct scene support
INSTRUCTION: She knew the Metabaron had nearly destroyed the Shabda-Oud when she was freed; she entered deployment with full awareness of what she was being sent against

BOUNDARY: Whether she retains awareness of or coordinates with her swarm copies during deployment is not shown — hold the question of distributed selfhood open; do not assume either continuity across copies or clean partition
BOUNDARY: What was specifically absent during imprisonment and returned during biomechanical reintegration — what the internal presence was — is not established in the source; hold this open
BOUNDARY: The outcome for Zombra after the incineration of all her copies on Flos is unresolved in the source — do not determine survival or death from this card
source_strategy: Single extracted record (Volume 17); no related peers or non-peer source records. Wiki provides Shabda-Oud lineage context; link matrix has no Zombra entries. Card is smaller and precise, bounded strictly to the source record. Organizing contradiction encoded as: her natural state is plural — imprisonment was erasure of self, not confinement of a self that remained intact. Irreducible refusal encoded as TRAIT. Three BOUNDARY facts protect the three explicit knowledge gaps from the source record.
